title: Cache-Dependency Fatal Failures
pattern: Structuring application logic such that cache misses are treated as fatal errors, or failing to size backend databases to handle total load when the cache is cold/evicted.
why_bad: If the cache layer goes down or is cleared (e.g., after a restart), the cold start traffic crashes the backend database, causing an unrecoverable cascading outage (cache stampede/cold start storm).
detection: Application crashes or returns critical failures upon missing cache entries, or failing to implement a fallback fetch route.
counterexample: Ephemeral caches containing only optional latency optimization data where misses safely fall back to DB.
fix: Provision the backend database to handle peak traffic load, and make cache misses fetch from DB.
source: *Software Engineering at Google*, "Managing State," p. 527; *Release It!*, p. 161.
